description: Why systems built from many unreliable machines are hard and how they are made to work: communication, time and ordering, replication and consistency, consensus with Paxos and Raft, fault tolerance and distributed storage, with the key algorithms implemented and tested under injected failures. Taught to the depth of a leading distributed systems course.
modelledOn: van Steen and Tanenbaum, Distributed Systems
Ongaro and Ousterhout, In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Raft)
Lamport, Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System
outcomes: Compare client-server, peer-to-peer and other architectures and explain the fallacies of distributed computing.
Build services with RPC and message queues and handle partial failure, retries and idempotency.
Reason about time with logical and vector clocks and order events across machines.
Explain replication strategies and consistency models and choose one for a given application.
Implement a Raft-based replicated log and explain Paxos and the FLP and CAP results.
Design fault-tolerant, scalable storage with partitioning, replication and transactions.

units.title: Introduction and architectures
topics: What a distributed system is; goals: scalability, availability, fault tolerance, transparency
The fallacies of distributed computing; partial failure; latency numbers every programmer should know
Client-server, multi-tier, peer-to-peer (structured and unstructured), microservices, serverless
Case studies: a mobile-money platform, a content delivery network, a university portal under load
Lab environment: running a cluster of processes or containers locally and injecting failures

units.title: Communication: RPC and messaging
topics: Sockets review; request-reply protocols; marshalling and interface definition languages
Remote procedure calls: stubs, semantics (at-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once myths), failures; gRPC and REST
Message-oriented middleware: queues, publish-subscribe, Kafka and RabbitMQ; delivery guarantees
Idempotency, retries, timeouts, backoff, circuit breakers
Group communication and multicast; gossip protocols

units.title: Time, clocks and ordering
topics: Physical clocks, drift, NTP and PTP; why wall clocks cannot order events
Lamport logical clocks and the happens-before relation; vector clocks and causality
Global snapshots (Chandy-Lamport) and distributed debugging
Hybrid logical clocks and TrueTime in Spanner

units.title: Coordination and naming
topics: Mutual exclusion: centralised, token ring, Ricart-Agrawala; leader election (bully, ring)
Distributed locks and coordination services: ZooKeeper, etcd; leases and fencing tokens
Naming and discovery: DNS, service registries, consistent hashing, distributed hash tables (Chord)
Membership and failure detection: heartbeats, phi-accrual, SWIM

units.title: Replication and consistency
topics: Why replicate; primary-backup, chain replication, multi-leader, leaderless (Dynamo-style quorums)
Consistency models: linearizability, sequential consistency, causal consistency, eventual consistency; read-your-writes and monotonic reads
The CAP theorem and PACELC; what partition tolerance really means
Conflict handling: last-writer-wins, version vectors, CRDTs; collaborative editing
Caching and invalidation; CDNs

units.title: Consensus: Paxos and Raft
topics: The consensus problem; the FLP impossibility result and what it means in practice
Paxos: proposers, acceptors, learners; the two phases; Multi-Paxos
Raft: leader election, log replication, safety, membership changes, snapshots
Implementing Raft and testing it with partitions, crashes and message loss
State machine replication; Byzantine fault tolerance (PBFT) and its use in blockchains

units.title: Fault tolerance and transactions
topics: Failure models: crash, omission, timing, Byzantine; redundancy and recovery
Reliable group communication and virtual synchrony
Distributed transactions: two-phase commit, three-phase commit, blocking; sagas and compensation
Checkpointing, logging and recovery; designing for graceful degradation

units.title: Distributed storage and file systems
topics: Distributed file systems: NFS, GFS/HDFS design and trade-offs
Key-value stores and wide-column stores: Dynamo, Cassandra, Bigtable; LSM trees
Partitioning (sharding), rebalancing, secondary indexes; replication across data centres
Spanner and globally consistent databases; NewSQL
Object storage and blob stores

units.title: Building and operating distributed systems
topics: Observability: distributed tracing, metrics, logs; debugging across machines
Load balancing, autoscaling, back-pressure, rate limiting
Security in distributed systems: authentication between services, TLS everywhere, zero trust
Capstone: a fault-tolerant replicated key-value store with a client library and chaos tests

schedule.title: Foundations and fallacies
schedule.exercise: Choose an architecture style for a campus portal under exam-week load and write half a page on which of the eight fallacies would hurt most.

tasks.title: Send requests across a three-hop topology while raising link latency from 5 ms to 300 ms and plot the end-to-end response time at each setting
Disable one link mid-transfer and record which of a client, a server and a router sees the partial failure first and what each observes
Compare client-server, peer-to-peer and microservice layouts for a file sharing app by counting messages and single points of failure per design

schedule.title: Case studies and the failure lab
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page failure analysis of a mobile-money platform, listing three components, how each can fail and what the customer sees.

tasks.title: Model a mobile-money platform topology with agent, gateway and ledger servers, send a transaction and trace each packet hop
Inject a 30 percent packet loss on the gateway link and measure the change in transaction completion rate over 100 requests
Place a cache or CDN node in a university portal topology and tune it to cut origin load by at least half under a given request mix

schedule.title: RPC and messaging
schedule.exercise: Compare REST, gRPC and a message queue for a payment notification service and state the delivery semantics each provides.

tasks.title: Trace a request-reply exchange between client and server in the packet view and list the marshalled fields in each message
Simulate an RPC with a lost reply under at-least-once and at-most-once semantics and count how many times the server executes the call
Simulate a publish-subscribe broker with three consumers where one fails mid-stream and compare at-most-once and at-least-once delivery counts

schedule.title: Reliability patterns and gossip
schedule.exercise: Design the retry policy for a payment call, giving timeouts, backoff schedule, idempotency key and when the circuit opens.

tasks.title: Retry a failing request with exponential backoff and jitter and plot the load seen by the server versus fixed-interval retries
Add idempotency keys so a retried payment is applied once, then run 50 duplicated requests and check the ledger total is correct
Spread an update through a 30-node gossip cluster with fanout 2 and measure rounds to full coverage, then vary the fanout and loss rate

schedule.title: Time, clocks and causality
schedule.exercise: Explain why two servers disagreeing by 200 ms can make a wall-clock ordering of bank transactions wrong, with an example timeline.

tasks.title: Run two drifting clocks with periodic NTP corrections and plot their offset to see how often it exceeds 50 ms
Assign Lamport timestamps to events across three processes in a given message diagram and list the pairs that are ordered by happens-before
Compute vector clocks for a six-message trace, identify the concurrent events and detect which two writes conflict

schedule.title: Coordination, naming and membership
schedule.exercise: Compare bully election, ring election and an etcd lease for choosing a leader in a five-node cluster, with message counts.

tasks.title: Run the bully election algorithm on five nodes when the leader fails and count messages until a new leader is announced
Place 10 nodes and 40 keys on a consistent-hash ring, add one node and count how many keys move
Tune a heartbeat failure detector with timeouts and a phi threshold against a simulated slow network and compare false positives and detection time

schedule.title: Replication and consistency
schedule.exercise: Choose a replication scheme for a school results database and justify the consistency level you offer to parents and to teachers.

tasks.title: Run a primary-backup group where the primary crashes and show which committed writes survive under synchronous and asynchronous replication
Classify five read/write histories as linearizable, sequentially consistent or eventually consistent, justifying each with the ordering evidence
Configure a three-replica quorum store with N=3, R and W settings, partition it, and show which settings reject requests and which return stale data

schedule.title: Conflicts and caching
schedule.exercise: Explain when last-writer-wins loses data and how a CRDT counter or set prevents it, using two concurrent edits as an example.

tasks.title: Simulate a cache in front of a database with TTL expiry and measure hit rate and stale reads at three TTL values
Merge concurrent updates from two replicas using last-writer-wins and version vectors and show which updates each rule loses
Implement a grow-only counter and an observed-remove set CRDT and verify replicas converge after random message reordering over 100 trials

schedule.title: Consensus: FLP, Paxos and Raft
schedule.exercise: Write a short explanation of why consensus is hard with failures, using the FLP result, and when Raft still makes progress.

tasks.title: Step through a consensus attempt among three nodes with one crashed node and show why a timeout is needed to guess the failure
Trace single-decree Paxos with two competing proposers through both phases and show which value is chosen and why
Run a Raft cluster of five nodes, kill the leader during replication, and show the new election and which log entries are preserved

schedule.title: Raft testing and state machine replication
schedule.exercise: Design five fault scenarios that a Raft implementation must survive and state the expected result of each.

tasks.title: Partition a Raft cluster into a majority of three and a minority of two, write to both sides, heal it, and verify the logs converge
Replicate a key-value state machine over Raft and show all replicas reach identical state after 50 commands with message loss
Run PBFT with four nodes and one Byzantine node sending conflicting values, and show the honest nodes still agree

schedule.title: Failure models, transactions and recovery
schedule.exercise: Describe the saga for booking a bus ticket with mobile money payment, including the compensating action at each step.

tasks.title: Classify seven observed behaviours as crash, omission, timing or Byzantine failures and choose the redundancy that tolerates each
Run two-phase commit across three participants, crash the coordinator after prepare, and show participants blocked until recovery
Design a saga for a mobile money transfer between two ledgers with compensation, then inject a failure at each step and verify balances stay correct

schedule.title: Distributed storage and sharding
schedule.exercise: Pick a storage architecture for photos, user profiles and transaction logs in a Ghanaian marketplace app and justify each choice.

tasks.title: Place files as chunks with three replicas across five nodes, fail one node and show the system restores the replication factor
Write 20 keys into an LSM-tree simulation, trigger memtable flush and compaction, and count reads and files touched for a lookup
Shard a table by hash and by range, then rebalance after adding a node and compare data movement and hotspot load on a skewed key set

schedule.title: Operations, security and capstone
schedule.exercise: Write a runbook for the capstone key-value store covering monitoring signals, failure drills and the order of recovery steps.

tasks.title: Trace one request through four services in a simulated network, find the slowest hop using per-hop latency and propose a fix
Configure a load balancer with health checks across three servers, take one down, and show traffic moving away without dropped requests
Run chaos tests against a replicated key-value store with crashes, partitions and delays and show that acknowledged writes are never lost
